history.period: Ancient (legendary origin); renovated 462 CE under Emperor Skandagupta
history.summary: NAME CORRECTION: the CSV's 'Shri Damodar Temple' is the documented Shri Radha Damodar Temple at Damodar Kund, on the road from Junagadh to Girnar Taleti. Legend ascribes the original temple to Vajranabh (Vrajnabha), grandson of Krishna (treating the '5000 years ago' claim as legend, not history); a historically grounded renovation was done in 462 CE during the reign of Gupta emperor Skandagupta. The pink-sandstone main temple has a Nij temple (65-ft shikhar) and Saloha Mandap (30.5-ft), with 32 arches and 84 carved pillars; the central shrine pairs Radha with four-armed Damodar (conch, discus, mace, lotus), plus adjacent shrines for Balarama-Revati and Ganesha. Damodar Kund and Revati Kund are within the premises; bathing in Damodar Kund is believed to absolve sins and grant moksha, and the 15th-century saint-poet Narsinh Mehta bathed here daily before worshipping Damodar. The complex is under the special care of the Government of Gujarat (Department of Archaeology). COORDINATE CONFLICT: Wikipedia lists 21.3132, 70.2910, which is ~20 km from the documented location near Bhavnath/Girnar Taleti, so it appears to be an error; coordinates used (21.5215, 70.4965) are APPROXIMATE, placing the temple on the Junagadh-Girnar road ~2 km from Bhavnath temple.

town_description: Junagadh is a historic city in Gujarat's Saurashtra region, nestled at the foot of Mount Girnar. Its past stretches from Ashoka's 3rd-century BCE rock edicts and the Uparkot Fort to the Nawabi-era Mahabat Maqbara, and it is a major pilgrimage hub for both Hindus and Jains.
